query: Let It Ride {Grisk sweeps your winnings into one neat stack and pushes it back into the middle of the table. "Let it ride," he says. "The second hand pays double. Most people stop here. Most people are dull."|Grisk is already shuffling. "Again?" he says, as if it were your idea. Your winnings sit in the middle of the table, waiting.|"Second hand," says Grisk, and the players at the next table stop pretending not to watch.} The new dealer is a woman who hasn't smiled once tonight. Let it ride {The unsmiling dealer turns her last card and looks at you properly for the first time. The pot is yours, and it's heavy.|You bluff on nothing and the whole table folds. Grisk laughs so hard he has to sit down.|You win the second hand by a single card. Somewhere behind you somebody says your name, which is not ideal.} {The dealer takes the hand without a flicker. Your winnings go back to the bank, and the walk home is very long.|You read her wrong, and she lets you know it. Grisk pats your shoulder. "That's the second hand," he says. "It's always the second hand."|The pot goes the other way. On the stair down, a lamp moves in the courtyard and you have to wait in the dark for it to pass.} Cash out {You stand, pocket your winnings and bow to the table. Grisk looks almost disappointed in you.|"Dull," says Grisk fondly, as you go. Your purse doesn't think so.|You leave while the leaving is good, and whistle all the way back to the castle, very quietly.}
